1 idea · Marketing

Customer lifetime value

Customer lifetime value (CLV) is the profit one customer brings over the whole relationship, not one sale. It tells a firm how much it can spend to win a customer.

A €12 monthly plan with a 40% margin earns €4.80 a month. If 4% of customers cancel each month, the average stays 1 ÷ 0.04 = 25 months. CLV = €4.80 × 25 = €120. Cut churn to 3% and they stay 33 months: CLV ≈ €160.

That is why Netflix, reporting Tuesday, watches churn as closely as new sign-ups.

Keeping customers longer can be worth more than winning new ones.
